clue.text: Unusual consul, one involved with Gaul, gets punishment in a body of poets

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters and the punishment inside the poetic word for a body

parts.note: corse is the old poetic word for a body or corpse

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of one and Gaul are mixed together

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a lash is a stroke of the whip, a punishment

explanation.surface: An odd Roman consul mixed up with the Gauls is flogged in front of a group of poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' is the anagram signal for one and Gaul, and 'in' puts that with the punishment inside the poetic body. The emperor Caligula reputedly planned to make his horse Incitatus a consul.
explanation.definitionFit: Caligula's horse Incitatus is the legendary animal the emperor meant to appoint consul, an unusual holder of that office.

clue.text: Vitally important neophyte, 16 of the 18 3

parts.note: cardinal means of chief importance, as in a cardinal rule
a neophyte is a beginner or new convert, a new man

explanation.surface: A newcomer of vital importance turns out to be the author of a famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references read 'creator of the Dream of Gerontius': John Henry Newman, later a cardinal, wrote the poem Elgar set to music; fittingly he was himself a convert.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal John Henry Newman wrote the poem The Dream of Gerontius, so he is its creator.

clue.text: Support for member on Uncle Tom's master's endless way

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the slave-owner's name is cut off

parts.note: Simon Legree is the cruel slave-owner in Uncle Tom's Cabin
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A support placed on the road of the brutal master from Uncle Tom's Cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-rest is a stool or rest that supports a leg, a limb or member of the body.

clue.text: See 18
Lewd student, American, upraising German air

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver's plate

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word up means it is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Luft is the German word for air

explanation.surface: A lecherous American student starts singing a German tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like a tune but is literal air, LUFT in German, which 'upraising' turns into TFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd and lustful are synonyms, both describing strong sexual desire.

clue.text: Fighting man takes second right, holding magazine

indicators.note: holding means the two letters grip the magazine's name between them

parts.note: The Oldie is a British humorous magazine for older readers

explanation.surface: A fighting man takes a moment to go right while carrying his ammunition clip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' suggests a soldier's ammunition, but it is The Oldie, a British magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a fighting man in an army.

clue.text: Animal at front of lake

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: An animal stands at the edge of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: An oxbow is a curved lake left when a meandering river cuts off one of its loops.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxbow is a type of crescent lake formed from a cut-off river bend.

clue.text: The only Scotsman to be wise?

definitions.text: The only Scotsman to be wise?

parts.note: solo means alone, the only one
mon is a Scots form of man, a Scotsman's address

explanation.surface: A jibe that only one Scot has ever been wise.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a 'solo mon' who was wise is the Old Testament king famed for his wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon is the Bible's byword for wisdom, so he is the one man proverbially wise.

clue.text: Given permission to execute debtor — anger apt to erupt

indicators.note: to erupt means to burst out violently, so these letters are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A debtor is cleared for execution, his fury about to burst out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'execute' suggests a hanging, but it means carrying out a will as executor.
explanation.definitionFit: When probate is granted, executors receive legal authority to administer a dead person's will.

clue.text: Looks at message of greeting

definitions.meaning: ... are good wishes sent in a letter, as in kind ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both views or eyes, and the good wishes sent at the end of a letter.

clue.text: Spherical, topless, like part of the ear

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word for spherical is removed

parts.note: globular means shaped like a globe, spherical

explanation.surface: A round, bare-chested figure resembling an ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spherical' looks like the definition, but it supplies GLOBULAR, which loses its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobular means relating to a lobe, and the earlobe is the soft part of the ear.

clue.text: Scot embracing me — that's what I was trying to say

definitions.text: that's what I was trying to say

indicators.note: embracing means the Scottish name hugs the word me inside it

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish first name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman hugging the speaker, who is struggling to explain himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to clarify or correct oneself, restating what one meant to express.

clue.text: Blondes Tennyson had his 18

definitions.meaning: Tennyson's poem is A Dream of ..., 18 being the word dream

explanation.definitionFit: Fair-haired women are blondes, and Tennyson's poem title is A Dream of Fair Women.

clue.text: Insecticide of a different ilk in horn

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the horn

parts.note: an antler is the branched horn of a deer

indicators.note: different means the letters of ilk take a new order

explanation.surface: Bug spray of some other sort kept in a horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horn' suggests a musical instrument, but it is a deer's; 'different' rearranges the ilk and 'in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ant killer is a poison used to destroy ants, a kind of insecticide.

clue.text: Weight that's white with spots

definitions.meaning: a small imperial unit of weight
the snow leopard, a pale spotted big cat

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a unit of weight and another name for the pale spotted snow leopard.

clue.text: Fuel merchant badly tailored at end of summer

indicators.note: badly means the letters of tailored are put together wrongly
end of means the final letter of summer is taken

explanation.surface: A petroleum dealer in an ill-fitting suit at the close of summer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil trader buys and sells oil, which is a fuel, so he is a fuel merchant.

clue.text: Scores 0, according to report

indicators.note: according to report means the word is heard spoken, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A team scores nothing, so the report says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks like a verb about goals, but it means notches or cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicks are small cuts or notches, the same as scores scratched into a surface.

clue.text: Gold beneath getting louder: take the food I made

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath means the gold comes below the rest

parts.note: cr is a musical abbreviation for crescendo, getting louder
to eat is to take food
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A rich, swelling invitation to eat a meal I cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take, eat' echoes the Communion words. The definition is what a maker would say of the thing made.
explanation.definitionFit: A creator is the one who can say of a work that he made it, its maker.

clue.text: Upper-class theologian was first to enter prize and got cosily placed

indicators.note: to enter means these pieces go inside the trophy

parts.note: a cup is a trophy, a prize
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
led means was in front, came first

explanation.surface: A posh scholar of religion, the winner, took the trophy and settled down snugly.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuddle up is to settle snugly against someone, cosily placed.

clue.text: End of the Spanish when French vicar's about

indicators.note: about means the French priest's title goes round the Spanish article

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest
los is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: The end of Spain's influence comes when a French priest arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A closure is a bringing to an end, a conclusion.

clue.text: Dying work provides end of good mortuaries

indicators.note: provides is read as supplies in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Death comes good for the undertakers, delivering a fine finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provides' signals the anagram: END OF, G and MORTUARIES are rearranged. Newman's poem, set by Elgar, follows a man's death and the soul's journey after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dream of Gerontius is Newman's poem about a man dying, a work about dying.

clue.text: Contradiction will drive one crazy

parts.note: to dement is to drive mad, with crazy completing the sense
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Being contradicted all the time would drive anyone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive ... crazy' together mean DEMENT, with 'one' between giving I at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A démenti is an official denial, a contradiction of a published statement.

clue.text: The Beckham christening question: O father, O mother, were our characters injured?

indicators.note: the letters of the words are damaged and put back in a new order

parts.words: O father, O mother, were our

explanation.surface: Parents fretting whether their names were hurt in the Beckhams' baby's naming.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beckhams named a son Romeo, so Juliet's famous line becomes a question at his christening.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's line asks why Romeo is Romeo, and a christening is where a child gets that name.

clue.text: Cultural disposition gives point to little sceptic

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
Thos is the short form of Thomas, as in doubting Thomas, the sceptical apostle

explanation.surface: A small doubter is given a sharp point.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or attitude of a culture or community.

clue.text: See 20
See 20
Lady to sing "Bread of Heaven" without a note

indicators.note: without means outside, so the food goes round the note

parts.note: manna is the food from heaven in Exodus, called bread from heaven
do (doh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A woman sings the Welsh hymn but leaves out a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread of Heaven' is a famous Welsh hymn, but here it is manna; 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is both Our Lady and the pop star, a lady who sings.

clue.text: Principal keeps soft reeds playing when up against a deadline

indicators.note: keeps means the main word holds the rearranged letters inside

parts.note: prime means principal, chief

indicators.note: playing means the letters of soft and reeds are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: The head of the orchestra holds the woodwind playing softly when time runs short.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pressed for time means having little time left, as when facing a deadline.
